text.tspan: When a being takes damage, it must lose that many composure tokens.
When composure runs out, the entity suffers a wound then refreshes
their composure and remaining damage carries over. This can cause a
single attack to inflict multiple wounds. Wounds are inflicted to a random
stat by rolling the wound die. If a hit inflicts multiple wounds, roll only
once and assign all wounds to the rolled stat.
When taking wounds, you may remove a token from either the available
or spent section on your character sheet and place it in the wounded.
Becoming wounded does not affect your stat values, your composure and
Hit Thresholds remain unchanged.
For example, a being with 4 Heft (and therefore 4 max composure)
suffers a massive hit for 9 damage. They remove 4 composure tokens,
then reset their composure, remove another 4, reset, and remove a final
token. This leaves them with 3 remaining composure and they suffer two
wounds. They roll to determine the wound location and roll Heft, so they
take two Heft Tokens, one from spent and one from available (as they had
only 1 in spent) and place them in wounded. If the attack had critically hit,
the attacker may have chosen to target Weird and killed this being.
4.9 Damage and Wounds
If any of your stats become entirely wounded, you die. You need a little of
everything to exist in this reality. There are other rare ways to die, such as
being pushed into a void or swallowed whole.
If you die, your miniature is removed from play and your cards are
discarded.I If you die, your miniature is removed from play and your cards
are discarded.
4.10 Death
Status effects are cards that you receive from attacks, abilities, and
terrain. They are temporary effects that can be positive or negative.
You may not have the same status effect equipped multiple times, and
status effects can have different effects on bosses. There is no limit to
the number of status effects you can have equipped.
5.3 Status Effects
Some abilities cause beings to lose composure:
This effect will reduce a beings current composure down to a minimum of
1, but it cannot inflict a wound, and does not count as damage.
5.4 Losing Composure
Many abilities grant temporary composure:
These are black temporary composure tokens that you can place on top
of your unspent composure tokens.
Temporary composure is always removed first, and is not replenished
when you refresh your composure. Temporary composure does not stack
though; if an effect would grant you more temporary composure than you
currently have, then you only then gain up to a total of that amount.
5.5 Temporary Composure
Some terrain pieces, and all sculpted beings, are Flammable. This keyword
means that the object can be set on fire and suffer the Burning status
effect. Things that are on fire have the following properties:
Any being that enters a Flaming hex, suffers the Burning status effect.
If the being is already Burning then they instead take 2 damage.
5.6 Flammable and Destructible
At the end of each players turn, they draw a card from the boss action
deck and place it in the next slot on the boss action board. At the end of
the round, when the starting player has taken a turn again, the boss will
perform all the actions on the boss action board in order.
The boss has Jazz, Heft, and Weird the same as you do, and takes damage
in the same way. When choosing how to perform a boss action, try to
make the boss act intelligently. The boss actions will explain how to
prioritise attacks and movement, but if there are ever situations where
the rules are not clear, favour the action that allows the boss to
effectively use its abilities on targets, or at least gets them in a better
position to do so in the future.
Some bosses have a unique mechanic that changes their core functionality
in some way, check the full rules for each boss in the boss book for
information on how to enact the bosses turn.
The boss will navigate terrain the same as players, paying additional hexes
of movement to go through obstacles. Some terrain applies differently
and will say so on the terrain card.
4.11 The Boss
You have the ability to push others using critical hits and card effects.
When you push a being, they must be pushed into a hex that is further
away from you than their starting hex. If a being would be pushed into a
solid object like a wall or another being, they instead they take damage
equal to the number of hexes they would have moved. This damage is
added onto the attack that caused the push and dealt simultaneously. If
the pushed being is pushed into another being then the receiver also
takes this additional damage.
5.2 Pushing
5- More Combat Rules
When you move in Sculpt, you may break the movement up between
other abilities. Each time you take a move action it gives you that many
hexes to use as you wish during your turn. For example, a being with a
move of 4 (the default) may take two move actions for 2 AP, use 3 hexes
to close a gap to a foe. Then make an attack for 2 AP, and then use the
remaining 5 hexes of movement to move away after the attack.
Some terrain impedes movement, such as cliffs and vines. If a hex would
take 2 movement hexes to move into, you must have 2 available (no
rounding). If you climb up or jump across a terrain feature, any hexes
moved must still be paid for in your movement. This is in addition to any
tokens or AP spent to interact with the terrain piece.
Some forms make your model larger. When moving a large character,
designate one hex on your model at the start of movement to count
hexes for, move that hex as far as you wish, then freely rotate the model
on the spot in your final position. If you are moving a large model into a
narrow space where it does not fit, each hex of movement costs double.
5.1 Movement
